First of all, I want to preface this by saying that I LOVE Voat so far. The smaller community, the leadership, the policies, the content... it's all nice, and I don't have any problems with any of it. And, by no means do I mean to disrespect this forum or anyone affiliated with it in any way.

Now, if at any point along this post you feel that I am bashing Voat, or I'm being condescending to the community, please refer back to the first three sentences. It's not my intention to offend anyone. I just want to create a dialogue for what I see happening here.

Now that that's out of the way...

I have been surfing Voat pretty constantly for the last couple of days (as constantly as the servers would allow), and I have noticed an air of... can we call it "fear?"... in every post. Nearly every post, every comment, and every user references Reddit in some sort of way, and some are even comparing things to Digg. It's not even exclusive to Voat: some outside articles are comparing Voat to Reddit. And it all seems (to me) to boil down to a few basic questions that everyone is tip-toeing around, and almost everyone is too afraid to ask outright:

  1. Is this forum going to be worthwhile and support good content?
  2. Are we going to become like Reddit/Digg in any capacity?
  3. What can we do to avoid becoming the next Reddit/Digg?

And these are all good questions in my opinion, and I fear that this site will never really reach it's full potential until we clear the air of the past and really move forward.

I have seen posts asking about the merits of getting rid of comment/post points or getting rid of downvoats in an attempt to curb reposts as well as junk content. I've seen discussions on posts about the merits/demerits of mocking Reddit openly. I've even seen posts asking us to stop referencing the sites which shall not be named altogether! People are posting screenshots of Reddit conversations about us, and there are very few posts that don't ask us why we left Reddit or what we think about Reddit/Pao. Honestly, if I wanted to read about Reddit or see what Reddit was doing without me, I'd go there myself...

There's a lot going on here, and it seems like we're already stagnant and not moving forward... so I suggest we attempt to work through this here, now, so that we can become the best we can!

FIRST

We have to discuss the idea of censorship (and this is going to hurt, and I know none of you want to hear it): It will exist in some sort of capacity... NOW, DON'T LEAVE YET!!! Please read the first three sentences, then come back here and let me explain... Either the mods/admins will have to take an active part in removing posts/comments, or the community will do it naturally through downvoats.

Reddit's original idea looked as if it were up to the community to control the content it saw. "Junk" posts or reposts would get downvoted and nobody would have to see it... essentially, the community would moderate itself and "censor" incorrect/troll posts out. The problem with this is that it became a giant circle-jerk. The community would only upvote certain content that agreed with a certain mindset and it would downwote anything that disagreed with that train of thought, and this became a MAJOR gripe of many users. So, using this exact same model, I don't honestly see an alternative outcome in ANY forum... none-the-less this one (read the first three sentences again, please).

Then there's the option of letting the mods/admins remove content for us. We can trust them to only remove reposts or incorrect/bad posts, but absolute power corrupts absolutely... I'm not saying that our current mods/admins are bad or that they shouldn't be trusted, I'm just saying that we should learn from our experiences with giving Pao power to remove posts at her discretion. Ultimately, we didn't like the admins removing posts for us, regardless of circle-jerk or not.

The point is that neither option appears to be the best for our goals. The upvotes work and don't work at the same time, and if we literally start where Reddit was a few years ago and expect a different outcome... what was it that Einstein said about insanity?

SECOND

If we continue to compare ourselves to Reddit, we will become Reddit. I know familiarity is a beautiful thing, and we're all put out by moving from a site we visited every minute of every day that we spent on the toilet, but I'm pretty sure we don't want another Reddit... we want something better for ourselves. The admins here have given us a GREAT starting point, but it's ultimately up to us to create something beautiful that works for us.

Yes, there are things that we liked about Reddit... that's why the majority of us were with them for so long... but there are also things we didn't like about Reddit, so we need to make those changes and become something different. We need to do what we need to do and move on... At least that my opinion, and your mileage may vary.

THIRD

It's not enough to complain about a problem... and it's not enough to point out the issues with the situation. I was always taught that, if you point out a problem, it's your job to actively figure out a solution. It's not enough to criticize everything.

So, since we're all slowly (and indirectly) pointing out the issues with the current system, I feel as if it's everyone's responsibility to find a solution to our "fears." We should all help make our own community the best that it can be.

So, now that I've ranted on my soapbox for so long (I apologize), here's the question: What should we do to answer/solve these questions and issues? What ideas do you have to assure we don't become another Reddit?

TL;DR: There seems to be some animosity between us and Reddit, and there shouldn't be. And, as long as there is, we will never be an independent site, nor will we become everything that our potential will allow us to be. So, how can we fix this and make Voat work?
What can we do to make this work?

Essentially, CCP should be a thing because it helps the community determine (and filter out) trolling and "junk" posts. We need it to differentiate brand new posts from troll posts (read the first link for more on this).

Also, total contribution points can be good to the individual user to show that he/she is doing good or bad. For instance, I can look at my total contribution breakdown and see that my single post hasn't done too badly... but if I look at it and see super low numbers or even negative numbers, I know I need to change the type of content I'm submitting. Good points can also be a motivating factor to posting good content: like trophies on the Playstation or achievements on the XBox... it makes you strive to be better for literally nothing (read the second link for more on this).

But a total contribution breakdown that's visible to the public only provides a measuring device for a pissing contest. Personally, I don't need to know that you have 0 SCP and 0 CCP right now. That doesn't affect me, and it doesn't affect how I Voat... so why am I able to see that?

So, personally, I don't feel like it needs to go away completely... but it does need to go away in a certain type of capacity.
